role.description: The role of the device's person, which it acts with.

oneOf.description: The key of the person whose device it is.

push.description: Whether the device gave a push token (device.push_token) that the daemon still holds.

kind.description: What the client said it is at device.redeem; null when it did not say. A mac or a server lends its machine. Absent on a daemon that does not serve it.

current.description: True in devices.list for the caller's own device; false in events. Absent on a daemon that does not serve it.

client.description: The client its last hello named (hello's client); null before one. Absent on a daemon that does not serve it.

lending.description: A mac's or a server's Run · Pause · Off (device.set): run starts new work on that machine, pause starts nothing new and lets what runs there finish, off is not lent. null for a phone or a browser. Absent on a daemon that does not serve it.

behind_s.description: Seconds since its copy last held all of the master's.

copy.description: The runner's copy of the board: when it last held all of the master's; null for a runner that keeps none (another person's, or one that has not pulled). Not on the master's own row.

Node.description: A machine of this master: its own, and the ones people lend it.

id.description: The machine's node id (DaemonStatus.machine.id on that machine).

person.description: The key of the person whose machine it is.

name.description: The machine's name, as it calls itself.

last_seen.description: When the master last heard from it: for its own row, the daemon's start.

master_number.description: The master number this machine last took; the master's own is the board's, raised by one each time the master moves (node.promote).

self.description: It is the machine this daemon runs on.

online.description: The master hears from it now; always true for the master's own row.

lending.description: run: the master starts new work there; pause: it starts nothing new there and what runs finishes. The master's own row is always run; a machine on off is not listed.

state.description: no_remote: the repo has no origin, so the workspace runs only on the machine that holds its folder. A failed one is tried again when the machine links again.

error.description: Git's word on a failed clone or fetch.

projects.description: Each workspace's repo on this lent machine, cloned from its remote when the machine links and when a workspace is added. Not on the master's own row, nor on a machine not linked since the master started.

lacks.description: Each agent that cannot start there now and why ("codex not installed", "full: 2 of 2 sessions", "it is set to pause"); a runner's row only.

device.description: The paired device (devices.list id) a lent machine joined as; null on the master's own row.

memory_max_gb.description: This lent machine's own cap on its agents' memory, in GB (device.set): at it, no new session starts there. null where agents_memory_max_gb applies, as it always does on the master's own row.

load.description: A lent machine's newest heartbeat's measures, 0 for one it could not read; null on the master's own row (DaemonStatus has its own) and before its first heartbeat since the master started.

battery.description: A lent machine runs on its battery now, from its newest heartbeat; null as load is.

version.description: Its Handline version: the master's own row the master's, a lent machine's from its newest heartbeat (null before its first since the master started). One not the master row's takes no work until it runs the master's build (node_build_auto, device.update).

door.description: Where it serves, or would serve, as master: addr (host:port) and fp (its certificate's sha256, "" for a plain door); null before it said.

set_aside.description: It was master, and a newer master outranked it: since when its own board is set aside, unchanged, and the master number that outranked it. null otherwise.

app.description: The Mac app around a lent machine's engine, as its heartbeat says: its version, and ready, the newer one its update channel has downloaded ('' for none); null for none (a server, a phone, an older app).

methods.name: devices.list
methods.summary: Paired devices with last seen and whether each is connected.

push_platforms.description: The platforms the daemon has push credentials for (config.yaml). Empty is push off: no device is sent a notification, whatever token it gave.

methods.description: The owner sees every person's devices, a member only their own.

methods.name: device.pair
methods.summary: Make a one-time pairing code.

schema.description: Seconds the code lives; default 300.
The person whose device it pairs (p<n>): the owner names one they invited (person.invite); a member only themself. The caller's own when left out.

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the door's self-made certificate, which a client pins; empty on a plain door and on Tailscale's own certificate, which is verified the normal way.

web_link.description: The pairing link, what the QR carries: http(s)://host:port/#pair=code, with &fp= the fingerprint on a self-made certificate. https on the Tailscale name when the tailnet has HTTPS (no fingerprint), http on it otherwise; a Wi-Fi door's link is for a Mac's app, which pins the fingerprint, as a Wi-Fi door serves no web page.

methods.description: Founder only. The code is single use and expires: `ttl_s` seconds (default 300, at most 600). The reply's `web_link` is the one link a device is given; on a self-made certificate it carries the fingerprint, which a client pins, refusing any other certificate. The link names Handline's pick: the Tailscale name while Tailscale is up, else the first LAN (Wi-Fi) address, served though network_addresses does not list it (not when the list is empty, and not while -advertise names the address); with neither, -advertise or the listener. With no door open it is refused, gate `network`. It is not replayed by request_id: a retry with the same request_id runs again and makes another code.
methods.x-note: The code is shown once and kept only as a hash; a second call makes a new code and leaves the first valid until it expires or is used.

methods.name: device.redeem
methods.summary: Trade a pairing code for a device token.

schema.description: What the client is: ios, android, web, desktop, or mac or server for a machine that lends itself, kept as Device.kind. Any other value is kept as null, so a newer client still pairs.
The machine's node id: required with kind mac or server, refused with any other. The device comes with that machine's node row, on off.

methods.description: The only method an unpaired network caller may call. A code that is wrong, expired or already used is refused, gate `pairing_code`, without saying which; too many wrong tries are refused, gate `attempt_limit`. A code redeems once: the token is in this one reply and never again, and the daemon keeps only its hash. `name` is how the device is listed. It is not replayed by request_id either: a retry runs again, and a code that was redeemed stays used, so the retry is refused. The wrong-code count for a redeem over the local socket is kept under the host '' (the empty string), since it has no address. A mac or a server whose node id this master already has is refused, gate `already_joined`. The device is the person's who made the code (device.pair).

methods.name: device.revoke
methods.summary: Cancel a device and close its connections at once.
methods.description: Cancels the device's token. Its open connections and terminal attaches are closed at once, its next call is refused (gate `unpaired`), and a device.revoked event is sent on the devices topic. Revoking a device that is not paired is not_found. A member revokes only their own devices (gate `person`).

methods.name: device.set
methods.summary: Set a lent machine's Run · Pause · Off and its own memory cap.

params.name: memory_max_gb
params.description: The machine's own cap on its agents' memory, in GB, at least 1; null puts it back to agents_memory_max_gb.

methods.description: Only the device's own person sets it; anyone else is refused, gate `person`. A device that is no mac or server that joined is refused, gate `kind`. run lists the machine in node.status and lets the master start work there; pause lists it as paused and the master starts nothing new there; off takes it out of node.status. A device.changed event is sent on the devices topic, and the nodes feed changes. It takes lending, memory_max_gb or both.

methods.name: device.update
methods.summary: Have a lent machine take the master's own build, and its Mac app install the version it has ready.
methods.description: The row's Update, for another person's machine or with node_build_auto off: the machine's next heartbeat answer names the master's build (node.heartbeat's build), which it takes and starts again on, as node_build_auto on does by itself. A Mac app with a newer version ready (node.status app.ready) installs it too (node.heartbeat's app_update). Only the device's own person updates it, gate `person`; a device that is no Mac or server that joined is refused, gate `kind`; gate `build` when it is offline, already runs the master's build with no app version ready, is another OS or architecture than the master (install Handline there), or the master serves no build of its own (also when this daemon hands none).

methods.name: device.make_master
methods.summary: Have one of the owner's Macs or servers take the master's place: "Make master" on its page.
methods.description: A device's page's Make master, on the master. Only the owner, for a machine of theirs that joined, gate `person`; a device that is no Mac or server that joined is refused, gate `kind`; one not linked to this master now, gate `node`. This master checks it can hand over to it as node.handover does (gates `copy`, `device`, `door`), and that machine checks it can take over as node.promote does (gates `state`, `board`, `door`, `copy`) and answers; then it does what node.promote does there: this master hands over (node.handover) and joins it as a runner. The answer comes before the move, which the page sees as the master going and the new one answering.

methods.name: device.push_token
methods.summary: A paired device gives the push token its OS gave it.

schema.description: An APNs token of a development build, which goes to Apple's sandbox host. Default false.

methods.description: Called by the paired device itself, after pairing and whenever its OS gives it a new token; the token is kept on that device's row in place of the one before. A connection that is no paired device (the local socket) is refused, gate `device`. The token is dropped when the device is revoked. devices.list shows whether a device has one (`push`).

methods.name: node.status
methods.summary: The machines of this master, its own first. Read only.

master.description: The master's node id and its number.

placement.description: Where each agent's next session starts and why (docs/story4-design.md section 7). Absent on a daemon that does not place agents.

agents.description: One row per agent of this home.

agent.description: The agent's key, as agent.set takes it.

device.description: The node id its next session starts on: the master's own while it stays.

why.description: Why it is placed so, in words a person reads ("heavy: check.sh 18 h this week", "heavy: ...; Studio: codex not installed, so it stays here", "pinned to Studio"); "" for a light agent on the master's machine.

heavy.description: Heavy by its last 7 days (over 2 h of heavy commands or a 6 GB peak): placed on the lent device with the most room.

heavy_s.description: Seconds its heavy commands ran in its last 7 days.

memory_peak.description: The most bytes its processes held in one minute in its last 7 days.

pin.description: The device it is pinned to (its device setting), kept on auto too; absent for none.

methods.description: The master's own machine and the machines lent to it on run or pause (device.set).

methods.name: node.forward
methods.summary: A runner's call for one of its agents, run on the master as that agent.

schema.description: The agent whose session made the call, as the runner proved it.
The call's own params, request_id included for a write.
The client the agent's hello named on the runner (hl).
The folder that hello was sent from.
The forwarded call's own result.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`), for an agent whose session the master opened there (gate `not_on_node`); never hello, a node.* or runner.* call, subscribe or unsubscribe (gate `method`). The answer comes back with its paths under the master's home made the runner's. A runner lent by a member calls it with that member's device token.

methods.name: node.turn
methods.summary: A runner's tracker tells the master one of its agents' turns.

schema.description: The agent whose session is on that runner.
The turn as the runner's tracker holds it: state (0 unknown, 1 working, 2 idle), at, doing, background, bg_known, settled, live (its session process is watched there), ended.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`), for an agent whose session is on that runner (gate `not_on_node`). Sent on each change of the turn and for every session when the link starts. The master's readers (the agent's view, an idle wait) see that agent as one of its own; when its session there stops or the link ends, its turn goes back to unknown.

methods.name: node.transcript
methods.summary: A runner sends the chat rows one line of an agent's session transcript holds.

schema.description: The agent whose session is on that runner.
When the line was written, epoch seconds.
Each {kind, body} as transcript_events keeps it: text, tool_use, tool_result (its output already cut to 16 KiB).

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`), for an agent whose session is on that runner (gate `not_on_node`). The master keeps the rows when chat_transcript_rows is on and drops them otherwise. Lines read while the master is away are not sent again.

methods.name: node.heartbeat
methods.summary: A runner says it is there: its version, load, sessions, accounts and what it has.

schema.description: The runner's Handline version: one that is not the master's takes no new session.
Its GOOS/GOARCH (darwin/arm64): the master hands its own build only to a runner of the same.
The machine's boot: another one means it restarted.
cores, load1, ram_total, ram_free and agents_rss (what its sessions' process trees use), as the runner read them.
Each session it holds: agent, handle, and the branch of its worktree with the commit last pushed (branch, pushed).

Each Claude account folder there logged in to an account: name, email, dir (its config dir, relative to the runner's home), reading (its newest usage reading: age_s, and windows of minutes, pct and reset) and login_failed (its login was refused even after a real turn).
What it has for an agent's work: clis, mcp, programs (of those the last answer asked about in check, the ones on its PATH), xcode, simulators.
The machine runs on its battery now.
Where it would serve as master: addr (host:port) and fp (its certificate's sha256, "" for a plain door). The master keeps it on the node row; a machine with none is not made the master.
The board it set aside when it was master and a newer master outranked it: since (unix seconds) and master (the number that outranked it).
Why it refused the master's build it was offered (a file whose sha256 is not the one named); its row says so in place of taking work.
The Mac app around this runner (a cluster engine's), as its shell wrote it: version, and ready when a newer one is downloaded.

stop.description: The agents of the sessions it holds that the master no longer places there: the runner pushes what each left to a rescue branch and stops it.

check.description: The programs its agents' MCP servers run, which its next heartbeat says it has or not (has.programs): an agent goes only to a runner with all it needs.

doors.description: To one of the owner's machines only: each of the owner's machines with a door, in the order they joined: {node, addr, fp}. A runner keeps it and, once its master is gone, asks each of them who is master now.

build.description: When the master wants it on its own build: it runs another version on the master's platform, and it is the owner's with node_build_auto on, or its row's Update was asked (device.update). version, and files: each {name, size, sum} (handlined and hl, sum their sha256). The runner reads each with node.build.read, checks it, keeps it under its home (build/, the newest only) and starts again on it; at a later start it runs the kept build while its master is on that version. Sessions there go on through the restart.

app_update.description: When its Mac app is to install the version it has ready: version, and auto (Auto on the owner's Mac with node_build_auto on, installed once no Handline window is open there) or not (its row's Update, device.update, installed at once). The app starts again on it; sessions there go on.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`). The runner sends one when its link comes up, then 15 s after each answer, so one is in flight at a time. The master keeps the newest in memory and the time as the node row's last_seen; a runner unheard for 60 s is offline, and after the reclaim time offline (node_reclaim_s, 30 minutes) its sessions are taken back. With the battery switch on (node_battery_switch), one that says it went on battery is set to Off from Run, and back to Run when it is plugged in.

methods.name: node.tokens
methods.summary: A runner sends the calls one of its accounts' transcripts gained.

schema.description: The account's name on that runner.
Each call as the token log reads it: session, req, ts, model, cwd, side and tokens {inp, cc, cr, out, thinking, cc1h}.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`). The master counts the calls in its usage under that account, each charged to the agent whose session made it; a call sent again counts once (by account, session and request). The runner moves its read positions only once the master has answered. Any linked runner may send for any account name: the runner is the person's own lent machine, so this is not checked against the node.

methods.name: node.copy.files
methods.summary: A runner pulls what its copy of the board lacks.

schema.description: The whole files its copy holds: {path, size}.
The files it is still receiving, with the bytes it has: {path, size}.

send.description: Pieces of the files it lacks, at most 512 KiB of data in all: {path, size, offset, data}; a file's last piece carries its sha256 sum, which the runner checks before it renames the file in.

gone.description: Paths the master's copy no longer has; given only with more false, so a runner never drops a file before what replaces it has arrived.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`). The board's copy is the folder Litestream writes on the master (board-copy in its home): each committed change within a second, a snapshot every hour, two hours kept. Only the owner's runners keep it: another person's is refused, gate `owner`, and drops any copy it holds; gate `copy` when the master keeps none now (the runner keeps what it holds). A pull that finds the runner already holding all of it sets the runner's copy in node.status.

methods.name: node.build.read
methods.summary: A runner reads a piece of a file of the master's own build.

data.description: Up to 512 KiB of the file from offset; empty past its end.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`). The files are the handlined this master runs and the hl beside it, as opened at its start; gate `build` when it serves none (one was not found beside it).

methods.name: node.promote
methods.summary: Make this machine the master: "Make this Mac the master".

number.description: The master number this machine takes.

handed_over.description: The master was reached and handed over, so nothing was lost; false: this machine took over from its copy, and what the master wrote after the copy's last pull is lost.

methods.description: On one of the owner's machines that joined, at its own socket (the founder at its terminal, `hl node promote`). No machine takes over by itself. With the master reached, it hands over (node.handover). Without it, this machine restores its copy of the board. Either way the copy becomes this machine's board, the master number goes up by one, and once the answer is sent the daemon starts again as master: the other runners find it by asking the owner's machines (node.heartbeat's doors) and join it with their own device tokens, and the old master, when it is back, sets its board aside and joins it as a runner. Gate `door`: it has no network door (handlined -listen); gate `copy`: it keeps no copy of the board yet.

methods.name: node.handover
methods.summary: The master hands over to the runner that is made the master.

number.description: The master number the runner takes.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`), from node.promote. The master refuses every write from then (gate `master`), stops its tick, writes its last changes into the copy and waits up to a minute until that runner's copy holds them all; then it answers, and once the answer is sent it joins that runner as a runner with its own device's token, its board set aside. A move that does not finish starts this master again.

methods.name: node.outranked
methods.summary: A machine of the owner says it is master with a higher number.
methods.description: From the master made so while this one was gone, each 15 s until it answers. Its word moves nothing: this master asks that machine at the door its own board has for it, pinned to its fingerprint, and joins it as a runner, its board set aside, only when the number there is the higher. A master also asks the owner's machines so at its start, before it fires a timer.

methods.name: node.launch
methods.summary: hl launch on a runner: the launch built on the master for that machine's home, and the files it starts with.

schema.description: The agent whose session asks, as the runner proved it.
session.launch_prepare's own params, as hl launch sent them on the runner.
argv, env and warnings as session.launch_prepare answers, their paths the runner's; files, each {path under the home, data in base64, mode}; agent_dir, the agent's folder under the home.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`), for an agent whose session the master opened there (gate `not_on_node`). Paths under the master's home are answered as the runner's. The only prompt file taken is the one the master wrote for the agent (gate `prompt_file`).

methods.name: node.agent_files
methods.summary: A runner's agent's memory and handoff note, as its session there wrote them.

schema.description: The agent whose session wrote them, as the runner proved it.
Each {path under the agent's folder, data in base64, mode}.
Paths under the agent's folder it removed.

methods.description: Only on a runner's link (gate `node`), for an agent whose session the master opened there (gate `not_on_node`); only memory/** and handoff.md inside the agent's folder (gate `path`).
